zhexuan.1.tier_reason: Core: granting the reader’s feeling first decides whether they read on, in any piece on a charged topic.
zhexuan.1.why: When a topic carries feeling, readers come in on guard. Start with reasoning and they hear a lecture; grant first that their grievance or anxiety is fair, and the wall comes down so the reasoning can get in. This step decides whether they finish the piece.
zhexuan.1.example: > [Demo] Trying all night to get a ticket and still not getting one: that tired, stifled feeling, anyone who has been through it knows. At the same time, it is worth asking: where did the tickets go?
zhexuan.1.breakdown:
- “tired, stifled”: the feeling is made specific, not a blanket “understandable”.
- “anyone who has been through it knows”: the writer stands beside the reader, not opposite as judge.
- “At the same time”: a parallel turn into thinking that avoids “but”, so the trust just built isn’t broken.
zhexuan.1.overdo:
We fully understand everyone’s anxiety, but anxiety solves nothing, and we must look at this rationally.

“Understand” is a formality, and the moment “but” arrives everything before it is cancelled; readers only hear that they are being taught.
zhexuan.1.when_not:
- When the topic carries no feeling (technical notes, pure information); forced acknowledgment seems affected.
- When the feeling itself isn’t legitimate, such as stirring up hostility; don’t endorse it.
zhexuan.1.exercise: On “working late into the night”, write two opening sentences that acknowledge the feeling, without the words “but” or “understand”.
zhexuan.1.check: After the first paragraph, does the reader feel the writer is on their side?
zhexuan.1.adjacent:
- zhexuan.12 Peer Positioning: acknowledging is a one-time move at the opening; peer positioning is the stance of the whole piece.
- guanfang.9 Dialectical Reply: that one grants the problem; this one grants the feeling.

zhexuan.2.tier_reason: Common: shifting a question up a level gets past loaded debates in commentary and essays.
zhexuan.2.why: Many debates are traps: however you answer, one side is offended. Ask at a different level and both sides are taken into a larger frame; readers get a sense of “so that’s how to think about it”. The truer the new question, the more convincing.
zhexuan.2.example: > [Demo] Rather than asking why young people don’t like phone calls, ask this: hasn’t communication today long stopped depending on the voice alone?
zhexuan.2.breakdown:
- “Rather than … ask this”: openly signals that the question is being replaced.
- The original question puts the blame on young people; the new one points to a change in how people communicate. Blame becomes observation.
- The new question can be answered with facts later, not left as a hanging rhetorical question.
zhexuan.2.overdo:
The problem was never you, it’s the times. It’s not that you didn’t try hard enough; the world changed.

It swaps the question without returning an answer and pushes everything onto “the times”; readers see at once that it is sophistry dressed as comfort.
zhexuan.2.when_not:
- When the original question is reasonable and has a clear answer; reframing is just evasion.
- When you can’t produce facts to support the new question.
zhexuan.2.exercise: Rewrite “why don’t children like reading nowadays” as a new question at a higher level that can be argued.
zhexuan.2.check: Does the new question explain more than the old one, and does the rest of the piece answer it?
zhexuan.2.adjacent:
- zhexuan.6 Elevate and Redefine: reframing changes the question, elevating changes the concept.
- zhexuan.8 Concrete-Abstract Sandwich: reframing sets the direction; the sandwich decides where the criticism lands.

zhexuan.3.tier_reason: Core: one precise, relatable number anchors an argument where feeling runs high, in any argumentative form.
zhexuan.3.why: Where feeling runs hottest, reasoning has the hardest time getting in, but facts can. A number precise enough that readers can measure it against their own lives turns feeling into understanding and gives the argument an anchor so it doesn’t drift.
zhexuan.3.example: > [Demo] A county hospital sees ×× patients a day but has only ×× general practitioners: worked out, one doctor has to see a whole train carriage of people in a morning. (Numbers are placeholders and must be replaced with traceable data.)
zhexuan.3.breakdown:
- “××”: real writing needs a source; without one, mark it [to verify].
- “a whole train carriage of people”: the total is converted into a unit readers can picture; that is what close to home means.
- The number sits right at the point of doubt and answers “just how stretched is it?”
zhexuan.3.overdo:
Plenty of data shows that the vast majority agree, and the problem has been greatly improved.

“Plenty”, “vast majority” and “greatly” are data at the level of concepts; none can be checked or felt.
zhexuan.3.when_not:
- When you can’t find a reliable source; better none than invented.
- In the lyrical passages of a human story; numbers break the warmth.
zhexuan.3.exercise: For “delivery riders have it hard”, find a relatable conversion and write one sentence with ×× as a placeholder.
zhexuan.3.check: Can readers measure this number against their own lives?
zhexuan.3.adjacent:
- guanfang.4 Data Alongside: that one presents change as a set; this one is a single precise, close-to-home point.
- zhexuan.4 Scene Hook: data handles understanding, the scene handles feeling.

zhexuan.4.tier_reason: Core: a concrete person or detail gives an abstract claim warmth, and stories are the flesh of evidence in every genre.
zhexuan.4.why: Readers can nod at an abstract claim but won’t remember it; an image stays. Readers see first and think after, and then the point can’t be held off. A story is the flesh on the chain of evidence and works across forms.
zhexuan.4.example: > [Demo] At the station ticket window, an old woman holds a slip of paper covered in writing: the steps her grandson taught her for buying a ticket. Step three is circled twice in pen. (The person is an invented example.)
zhexuan.4.breakdown:
- “a slip of paper covered in writing”: one object tells you she can’t use a phone.
- “circled twice”: the anxiety is hidden in the detail; the writer doesn’t need to point it out.
- The image leads straight to the point (the digital divide), not emotion for its own sake.
zhexuan.4.overdo:
At that moment tears blurred his eyes, and he thought of his faraway home, of the dreams he once had …

All stock emotion, not a single verifiable detail, and the story is cut off from the point.
zhexuan.4.when_not:
- When the detail can only be invented yet would pass as true; leave it out or mark it as an example.
- When readers need a quick conclusion (debunking a rumor, say); a scene slows things down.
zhexuan.4.exercise: For “old people living alone”, write a two-sentence scene with only one object and one action.
zhexuan.4.check: If you delete this scene, does the point lose its persuasive force?
zhexuan.4.adjacent:
- guanfang.5 Small to Large: that one leans toward holding up a grand theme.
- zhexuan.8 Concrete-Abstract Sandwich: the scene is one of the materials of the concrete layer.

zhexuan.5.tier_reason: Common: breaking a vague target into countable types sharpens criticism in commentary and explainers.
zhexuan.5.why: Railing at “chaos” in general gives readers nothing to check against; split it into three to five mutually exclusive types and the criticism has a bullseye, which readers can even use to check themselves and pass on. The more precise the breakdown, the sharper the piece.
zhexuan.5.example: > [Demo] A round of “sentiment marketing” goes in roughly three steps: first tell a story that softens the heart, then manufacture a “last chance, limited time”, and finally close the net with “not buying means you don’t support us”.
zhexuan.5.breakdown:
- “three steps”: stages that don’t overlap, in a clear order.
- Every step is an action readers can match to something they have seen.
- After the breakdown, name the shared fault (using feeling as leverage); don’t stop at a list.
zhexuan.5.overdo:
The current problems are mainly: first, inadequate understanding; second, ineffective measures; third, incomplete implementation; fourth, insufficient supervision.

The types overlap, there isn’t one case, it’s an official-document list readers can’t check against.
zhexuan.5.when_not:
- When the target is already clear and single; forced splitting looks like padding.
- When you can’t give a real example for each type.
zhexuan.5.exercise: Break “clickbait” into three types that don’t overlap, and write a sample headline of your own for each.
zhexuan.5.check: Could the types be swapped for one another? If so, they aren’t mutually exclusive.
zhexuan.5.adjacent:
- zhexuan.8 Concrete-Abstract Sandwich: the breakdown supplies the concrete target; the sandwich makes sure there is a protective layer.
- guanfang.8 Rising Parallels: parallelism pushes forward with matching structures; a breakdown sorts side by side.

zhexuan.6.tier_reason: Common: redefining a misused word with “not A, but B” clears a debate in any argumentative piece.
zhexuan.6.why: Debates often get stuck on a word that has been contaminated. Redefine it, and readers don’t have to pick right or wrong; they see a truer meaning, and those who were labeled get a clean word.
zhexuan.6.example: > [Demo] Being “good at managing a household” doesn’t mean refusing to spend on anything; it means knowing where the money should go.
zhexuan.6.breakdown:
- “doesn’t mean refusing to spend on anything”: first take apart the misunderstanding in the old definition.
- “it means knowing where the money should go”: the new definition is more accurate and easier to live by.
- The second half is more concrete than the first; rebuilding takes more effort than taking apart.
zhexuan.6.overdo:
Success isn’t success but a state of mind; effort isn’t effort but a choice.

“But B” is emptier than “not A”; the new definition isn’t truer, it’s a tongue-twister.
zhexuan.6.when_not:
- When the concept hasn’t been contaminated; redefining it just manufactures a talking point.
- When the new definition risks whitewashing.
zhexuan.6.exercise: Redefine “Buddha-like” (佛系, a shrug at striving) with “not … but …”, with a concrete behavior in the second half.
zhexuan.6.check: Would an ordinary reader accept the new definition as more accurate?
zhexuan.6.adjacent:
- zhexuan.2 Reframe the Question: changes the question.
- zhexuan.10 Compress to Aphorism: redefinitions are often pressed into aphorisms, but an aphorism isn’t always a definition.

zhexuan.7.tier_reason: Common: alternating past and present cases gives depth to conclusions in commentary and essays.
zhexuan.7.why: Talk only of the present and a view sounds like one person’s opinion. Alternate past and present, and readers see the same pattern recur; “I think” becomes “history shows again and again”, and the new phenomenon gains grounds for being understood.
zhexuan.7.example: > [Demo] When cameras became common, people worried painters would lose their jobs; painters didn’t disappear, and new ways of painting appeared. Today’s worries about new tools are worth placing on the same long line.
zhexuan.7.breakdown:
- The historical anchor is a familiar, uncontroversial technological change, no showing off learning.
- “didn’t disappear, and …”: gives history’s outcome.
- “worth placing on the same long line”: builds a clear logical bridge so past and present serve one point.
zhexuan.7.overdo:
From ancient times to today, from East to West, from farming civilization to industrial civilization, humanity has always moved forward through change.

Both ends are empty concepts without one concrete case; the contrast has slogans and no bridge.
zhexuan.7.when_not:
- Don’t use historical facts you aren’t sure of as anchors.
- When the historical analogy is plainly strained; forcing it weakens the argument.
zhexuan.7.exercise: For “young people love saving money”, find a historical parallel you know for certain, write one sentence for the past and one for now, and a linking sentence.
zhexuan.7.check: Between the past and present passages, is there one sentence saying plainly what they both show?
zhexuan.7.adjacent: - guanfang.3 Historical Depth: one stretch of history as grounding; here past and present alternate several times.

zhexuan.8.tier_reason: Signature: aiming at the execution while protecting the principle is how this style dares to touch a topic without overturning.
zhexuan.8.why: The more concrete the target, the more precise and the safer the criticism; at the same time a layer of abstract principle catches it, so readers know the writer opposes the practice, not the foundation. This is the structural secret of daring to touch something without overturning.
zhexuan.8.example: > [Demo] What deserves criticism is the specific practice of turning “lightening the load” into three more forms to fill in; the original aim of lightening the load is precisely to give time back to children.
zhexuan.8.breakdown:
- “three more forms to fill in”: the target lands on the operational level of execution.
- “the original aim of lightening the load”: the abstract protective layer, showing the principle isn’t rejected.
- Both layers are present at once, so the criticism has an edge and also a limit.
zhexuan.8.overdo:
In the end all of this is caused by the system and capital; the whole society is sick.

The target spreads into “the system” and “society”, with no concrete object and no protective layer; it crosses the line at once and is only venting.
zhexuan.8.when_not:
- Purely positive narratives that need no layer of criticism.
- When you can’t produce a concrete target; better not to criticize.
zhexuan.8.exercise: On “box-ticking check-ins”, write two sentences: one criticizing a specific practice, one stating the principle being protected.
zhexuan.8.check: Could a specific department or practice claim the criticism, and is there one explicit line of protection?
zhexuan.8.adjacent:
- zhexuan.5 Deconstruct to Enumerable: supplies the concrete target.
- guanfang.9 Dialectical Reply: answers after granting the problem, without necessarily separating levels.

zhexuan.9.tier_reason: Common: a three-line close gives a structured stance readers can carry away, in columns and speeches.
zhexuan.9.why: After a piece, readers need something to take with them. Three lines are easy to remember and pass on; if each adds a stance, readers leave with a clear attitude rather than a feeling.
zhexuan.9.example: > [Demo] Toward old crafts, a little more patience; toward new ways of playing, a little more curiosity; toward people still finding their way, a little more tolerance.
zhexuan.9.breakdown:
- Three different objects: old crafts, new ways, people finding their way; each line adds something.
- “a little more …”: matching structures keep the rhythm even.
- A clear stance on both tradition and innovation, not fence-sitting.
zhexuan.9.overdo:
Let us have a little more understanding, a little more tolerance, a little more forbearance.

Three lines say one thing; understanding, tolerance and forbearance are near-synonyms, with no added stance.
zhexuan.9.when_not:
- When the piece has just used a parallel series; another at the end repeats it.
- When the stance hasn’t yet been argued in the body.
zhexuan.9.exercise: Write a three-line close for a piece on “simpler weddings”, each line addressed to a different party.
zhexuan.9.check: Delete any one of the three lines: is the stance clearly incomplete?
zhexuan.9.adjacent:
- guanfang.8 Rising Parallels: lifts the argument mid-way.
- guanfang.10 Call to Action: gives an action; this gives a stance.

zhexuan.10.tier_reason: Signature: one line that holds outside its context is what readers carry when they share the piece.
zhexuan.10.why: What can be screenshotted can spread. A well-compressed line is the crystal of the whole argument, and it is what readers take when they share. It has to grow at a node of the argument and stand up to scrutiny.
zhexuan.10.example: > [Demo] The recommendation algorithm remembers what you clicked, but not why you stopped.
zhexuan.10.breakdown:
- A contrast: “remembers what you clicked” against “not why you stopped”.
- Posted on its own it still holds, without depending on context.
- It must come after the piece has argued how recommendations work, or it floats.
zhexuan.10.overdo:
No road you walk is wasted, every step counts; if you bloom, the breeze will come.

The lines have nothing to do with the argument; it is a pile of maxims, greasy and unable to bear scrutiny.
zhexuan.10.when_not:
- Stop once a piece has more than three.
- When accuracy is sacrificed for polish.
zhexuan.10.exercise: Compress a passage of argument you have written into one line of no more than twenty words, and check whether it stands alone.
zhexuan.10.check: Would this line hold up posted on its own, and did the piece argue for it first?
zhexuan.10.adjacent:
- guanfang.6 Four-Character Phrases: solemn summary, not meant to spread on its own.
- zhexuan.6 Elevate and Redefine: a definition can become an aphorism, but an aphorism isn’t always a definition.

zhexuan.11.tier_reason: Signature: this topic-choosing calculation, collective feeling times an unanswered moment, is what drives this style’s reach.
zhexuan.11.why: Readers need a piece most when feeling is rising and no one has explained it. A piece that catches the feeling and offers understanding and a way forward at that moment gets shared widely. That isn’t luck; it is judging the timing.
zhexuan.11.example: > [Paraphrase] This style often publishes in application season, exam season, or the week a word floods social media, answering head-on the feeling everyone is discussing but nobody has explained.
zhexuan.11.breakdown:
- Test one: how many people are going through this feeling right now?
- Test two: is any authoritative voice responding at this moment?
- Test three: can I give a complete answer, “acknowledge → understanding → a way forward”? Only start writing if all three hold.
zhexuan.11.overdo:
Topic X is trending! Today let’s talk about it too. What do you think? Leave a comment below.

It only chases the trend with nothing added; someone has already caught the feeling and you are just joining the crowd.
zhexuan.11.when_not:
- With sensitive events beyond what public authoritative statements can characterize.
- When you can’t offer a way forward; chasing the trend only adds noise.
zhexuan.11.exercise: List three collective feelings you noticed this week, score each against the three tests above, and pick the one most worth writing.
zhexuan.11.check: Can each of the three tests be answered “yes” in one sentence?
zhexuan.11.adjacent: - zhexuan.1 Acknowledge: arbitrage governs the timing of the topic; acknowledging governs the first move on the page.

zhexuan.12.tier_reason: Core: treating readers as fellow thinkers removes the lecturing tone, and every genre benefits from that stance.
zhexuan.12.why: A lecturing tone is argument’s worst enemy. Use “we” and “consider”, and genuinely let readers keep their own view; they feel respected and are willing to keep thinking with you.
zhexuan.12.example: > [Demo] Consider our own parents: they too were once told “this generation is hopeless”. As for how to see it this time, the answer is left to each of us.
zhexuan.12.breakdown:
- “Consider”: an invitation, not an order.
- “our own parents”: writer and reader stand in the same generation.
- “the answer is left to each of us”: the choice is really handed over.
zhexuan.12.overdo:
Each of us should realize that we must change our thinking and we must learn gratitude.

The “we” is only “you should” in other words; the stance was fixed long ago, and the equality is fake.
zhexuan.12.when_not:
- Formal notices and regulatory documents that need clear requirements.
- On questions where the stance is settled and not open to debate; pretending to be open is hypocritical.
zhexuan.12.exercise: Rewrite “you should treasure your time” as two sentences in peer positioning.
zhexuan.12.check: Delete “we”: is the sentence an order? If so, the stance is fake.
zhexuan.12.adjacent:
- zhexuan.1 Acknowledge: the opening move.
- guanfang.10 Call to Action: uses “we” to rally at the end; here it is a stance through the whole piece.
